narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A Javanese dance historian or local Salatiga cultural ambassador.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

episode_1.title: Meet Jurit Ampil Kridha Warastra Dance

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Concubine Archers of Salatiga
This is Jurit Ampil Kridha Warastra Dance. 18th century.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (vaomwDA1VSE)
Title card: Jurit Ampil Kridha Warastra Dance · Indonesia · 18th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance commemorates the 17 March 1757 Treaty of Salatiga, where Mangkunegara I showcased his elite female military unit, the Jurit Ampil, to demonstrate his military strength.
on_screen: Map: Indonesia · Southeast Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance serves to convey the historical military discipline of the concubines of Mangkunegara I during the 18th-century political shifts in Java.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is a free-style performance that can be executed by soloists, pairs, or groups.
It blends classical Surakarta court dance with the movements of the Prajuritan folk martial dance.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (vaomwDA1VSE)
Signature moves — MISSING
Formation: Flexible: solo, pairs, or groups.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music uses a Javanese gamelan in the pelog scale, featuring instruments such as the gender, kendhang, demung, saron, kenong, kempul, and gong.
Compositions include lancaran, srepeg, and palaran.
Listen for the gender, kendhang, demung, saron.
A Javanese gamelan ensemble playing in the pelog scale, characterised by the percussive interplay of metallophones and drums.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear a blue short-sleeved shirt with gold embellishments, a belt, a dodot, and knee-length trousers.
Accessories include a small bun with a golden crown and weapons: bow, quiver, arrow, and dagger.
